tldr: MobileGPT is an LLM-based mobile task automator equipped with a human-like hierarchical app memory that decomposes tasks into reusable sub-tasks, enabling accurate, efficient, and adaptable task automation.
contributions: Introduced MobileGPT, an LLM-based mobile task automator that emulates human cognitive processes (explore, select, derive, recall) for mobile task learning and execution.
Designed a three-level hierarchical memory structure (tasks, sub-tasks, actions) with function-call formatted sub-tasks for efficient storage and flexible retrieval.
Developed a dual-strategy correction mechanism combining self-correction through feedback generation and human-in-the-loop (HITL) task repair.
Evaluated MobileGPT on 185 tasks across 18 mobile apps, demonstrating superior performance over Auto-Droid and AppAgent.
methods: MobileGPT converts mobile screens into simplified HTML representations using Android Accessibility Service, reducing tokens by an average of 84.6%. It operates via an Explore-Select-Derive-Recall cycle: the offline Explore phase uses random explorer and user trace monitor to pre-collect sub-tasks per screen; the Select phase chooses relevant sub-tasks from memory; the Derive phase incrementally generates low-level actions (click, input, scroll). A hierarchical transition graph stores memories, with sub-tasks parameterized in function-call format. Self-correction detects errors like invalid UI interactions and screen loops, while HITL repair allows users to intervene at Explore, Select, or Derive stages.
results: MobileGPT achieved an 82.7% task completion rate on new tasks, outperforming Auto-Droid by 8% and AppAgent by 15.3%. It achieved a 98.75% success rate in adapting learned tasks to new instructions with different parameters. Recall of learned tasks reduced task completion time by 62.5% and LLM query costs by 68.8%. Screen representation pruning reduced token counts by an average of 84.6%. A usability study with 23 participants confirmed the effectiveness of the HITL repair mechanism.
limitations: LLMs are inherently non-deterministic and unpredictable, requiring error correction mechanisms.
Certain critical actions (e.g., sending a message, deleting a contact) cannot be undone once executed, requiring manual app restoration.
The offline Explore phase, while conducted locally, could benefit from server offloading for enhanced efficiency.
